title: Why green bean and almond Works So Well Together
flavorProfile: The crisp, slightly sweet vegetal notes of green beans complement the buttery, nutty richness of toasted almonds, creating a balance of savory umami from the beans’ natural glutamates and the Maillard‑derived flavors of the nuts, while a hint of sweetness from both ingredients rounds out the profile.
nutritionalSynergy: Green beans provide vitamin C, folate, and iron; almonds supply vitamin E, magnesium, and healthy monounsaturated fats. The fat in almonds enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamin E and helps solubilize carotenoids from the beans, while vitamin C from green beans improves non‑heme iron uptake from both foods, creating a synergistic micronutrient boost.
prepTechniques: Trim and blanch the green beans in salted boiling water for 2‑3 minutes, then shock in ice water to retain color and crunch.
Toast sliced or slivered almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden and fragrant, stirring frequently to avoid burning.
Toss the blanched beans with the toasted almonds, a drizzle of olive oil, lemon zest, and a pinch of sea salt; serve warm or at room temperature.

faq.a: Cool the dish to room temperature, then transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days; reheat gently in a skillet or microwave, adding a splash of water if needed to revive texture.
